suspect:piers_dunne: Piers Dunne stood on the slipway with his hands in his pockets. His oilskin was dry but his boots had a tide line above the ankle.
event:tidal_window: The sea cave floods completely within forty minutes of low slack. Anyone inside without a boat would not survive the rising water.
motive:fishing_economy: The harbour depends on a fishing quota allocated by catch weight. Dunne's boats had exceeded the annual limit by three hundred tonnes.
suspect:gill_rowan: Gill Rowan crewed Dunne's lead boat and knew the cave passages. His salt-stained jacket hung in the chandlery beside a coil of new rope.
suspect:harbour_master: The harbour master signed the daily logbook and controlled slipway access. His entries for the night in question are unusually brief.
suspect:malcolm_crewe: Malcolm Crewe ran the fish market and handled the catch manifests. His fuel receipts showed a boat trip on the night of the death.
suspect:fiona_cross: Fiona Cross was the victim's sister and had argued with Dunne over access permits. Her boots carried salt from the breakwater path.
suspect:coastguard_bell: Coastguard Bell patrolled the coast path and logged vessel movements. His camera housing was found empty in the research cabin.
suspect:dr_anne_webb: Dr Anne Webb supervised the marine survey that measured fish stocks. Her report was due at the ministry by the end of the month.
location:dunne_harbour: Dunne Harbour sits in a granite cove facing west. The slipway drops steeply and the sea wall holds back spring tides.
location:sea_cave: The sea cave opens at the base of the headland and runs sixty metres inland. At low slack the floor is exposed for forty minutes.
location:fish_market: The fish market opens at five and closes when the catch is weighed. The scales are calibrated weekly and the logbook sits on the counter.
location:coast_path: The coast path follows the cliff edge from the harbour to the headland. Fog rolls in from the west without warning.
location:research_cabin: The research cabin stands on the cliff above the cave entrance. Sample jars line the shelf and a tide chart is pinned to the wall.
location:slipway: The slipway is the only launch point inside the harbour wall. The concrete is scraped by keels and the bollards hold mooring lines.
location:breakwater: The breakwater extends fifty metres from the harbour mouth. At high tide only the top course of stone is visible.
location:chandlery: The chandlery sells rope, paint, and engine parts to the fleet. A board inside the door lists the tide times for the week.
object:sample_jars: Six sample jars from the research cabin contain water from the cave. Three show elevated nitrogen levels consistent with fish waste.
object:logbook: The harbour logbook records all vessel movements by time and berth. The entry for the night of the death has been written over in darker ink.
object:mooring_rope: A mooring rope on the slipway bollard shows a clean cut six inches from the splice. The fibres indicate a sharp blade, not wear.
object:quota_records: The quota records for Dunne's fleet show annual catches within limits. An independent audit found discrepancies of three hundred tonnes.
object:water_samples: Water samples from the cave show elevated nitrogen and phosphate levels. The contamination is consistent with large-scale fish processing waste.
object:visitor_permit: Ellen Cross held a research access permit for the cave system. The permit was valid for daylight hours only.
object:engine_key: The engine key for Dunne's lead boat was found in the chandlery drawer. The ignition showed signs of recent tampering.
object:salt_stain: A salt stain on the slipway bollard extends above the normal tide line. The pattern suggests a rope was pulled tight against wet stone.
object:catch_manifest: The catch manifest for March shows three landings not recorded in the harbour logbook. The weights are listed in a different hand.
object:camera_housing: An underwater camera housing was found empty in the research cabin. The lens mount shows scratches consistent with forced removal.
object:survey_report: The marine survey report concludes that fish stocks have declined by forty percent. The decline correlates with unreported catches from Dunne's fleet.
object:fuel_receipt: A fuel receipt from the chandlery shows diesel purchased at 22:00 on the night of the death. The buyer is listed as cash.
object:anchor_chain: An anchor chain from Dunne's boat was shortened by two links. The removed links were found in the tool locker.
emotion:salt_roughness: He spoke without looking up from the rope he was coiling. His answers came in the same flat tone as the harbour wind.
emotion:steady_gaze: She held the inspector's eye without blinking for a count of five. Her hands rested on the breakwater rail.
emotion:clipped_denial: Every question about the quota was met with one word or fewer. He did not sit down during the interview.
emotion:practised_sorrow: He removed his cap and held it against his chest. His condolences were fluent and his eyes moved to the slipway.
emotion:turned_away: She turned toward the window when the survey report was mentioned. Her hand moved to the sample jars on the shelf.
emotion:hard_silence: He said nothing when shown the fuel receipt. His jaw tightened and he looked out toward the breakwater.
modifier:rope_frayed: The mooring rope was cut cleanly but the splice end showed deliberate fraying. Someone had disguised the cut as natural wear.
modifier:quota_exceeded: The independent audit found three hundred tonnes above the permitted annual catch. The excess was landed at night and sold through the market.
modifier:cave_flooded: The cave floods completely within forty minutes of low slack turning. The water rises from the back passage first.
modifier:engine_disabled: The engine ignition wire was disconnected at the starter relay. The disconnection required a spanner and knowledge of marine engines.
modifier:fog_bank: A fog bank rolled in from the west at half past three. The coast path was invisible from the harbour by four.
modifier:slipway_scraped: Fresh keel scrapes on the slipway concrete show a boat was launched between two and four in the morning. No launch was logged.
modifier:manifest_altered: The catch manifest for three landings was written in a hand that does not match the harbour master's. The ink is newer.
modifier:salt_on_jacket: Salt crystals on Dunne's oilskin jacket formed above the waterline. The pattern indicates full immersion followed by air drying.
modifier:chain_shortened: Two links were removed from the anchor chain using a bolt cutter. The cut faces show fresh steel.
modifier:boot_salt_ring: A salt ring on Fiona Cross's boots extends to mid-calf height. The ring matches the water level at the cave mouth during rising tide.
action:boat_launched: A boat was launched from the slipway between two and four in the morning. The keel scrapes are fresh and the bollard rope is slack.
action:rope_cut: The mooring rope was cut with a sharp blade close to the splice. The cut was made to look like fraying from wave action.
action:records_falsified: Three landing records were added to the catch manifest after the original entries. The ink and handwriting differ from the standard log.
action:cave_entered: Ellen Cross entered the sea cave at low slack with her sample jars. She was expected back at the research cabin within the hour.
action:engine_tampered: The engine ignition was disabled by disconnecting a single wire. The boat could not start without reconnecting it.
action:permit_revoked: Dunne attempted to revoke Ellen Cross's research permit two weeks before her death. The harbour committee overruled him.
action:samples_collected: Ellen Cross collected water samples from three points inside the cave. The nitrogen readings confirmed illegal fish waste discharge.
action:chain_released: The anchor chain was released while the boat was moored at the cave entrance. Without the chain, the boat drifted on the rising tide.
action:logbook_amended: The harbour logbook entry for the night of the death was overwritten in darker ink. The original entry is partially visible beneath.
time:low_slack: Low slack occurred at 02:14 on the morning of the death. The cave floor was exposed for approximately forty minutes.
time:rising_flood: The rising flood began at 02:54 and reached full cave height by 03:34. The water enters from the back passage first.
time:dawn_discovery: The coastguard found Ellen Cross at dawn when the tide receded. Her body was at the far end of the cave with sample jars beside her.
time:market_closing: The fish market closed at nine on the morning after the death. The catch manifest had already been filed.
time:quota_deadline: The annual quota report was due at the ministry by the end of March. The audit was triggered by Ellen Cross's preliminary findings.
motive:overfishing_cover: If the survey report reached the ministry, Dunne's fleet would lose its licence. The excess catch was worth more than the boats.
motive:survey_suppression: Ellen Cross's marine survey documented the stock decline caused by overfishing. Her data directly implicated Dunne's landing records.
motive:licence_loss: A quota violation finding would result in the revocation of all five fishing licences. The harbour economy depends on Dunne's fleet.
motive:subsidy_fraud: Malcolm Crewe received a subsidy based on reported catch volumes. If the true figures emerged, the subsidy would be clawed back.
motive:family_livelihood: Gill Rowan's family has crewed Dunne's boats for two generations. Without the fleet, the family has no income.
witness:ferry_captain: The ferry captain saw a boat heading west from the harbour at half past two. The running lights were off.
witness:bait_seller: The bait seller opened at four and saw the slipway bollard rope hanging loose. He did not report it.
witness:dock_hand: The dock hand found fresh keel scrapes on the slipway at five. He assumed a boat had launched for the early tide.
witness:pub_landlord: The pub landlord served Dunne and Crewe at nine the previous evening. They spoke quietly and left separately before closing.
witness:lifeboat_crew: The lifeboat crew was not called that night. They noted the fog bank from their station window at half past three.
event:ellen_cross_discovered: Ellen Cross was found in the sea cave at dawn with her sample jars beside her. The tide had receded and the floor was wet.
event:spring_survey: The spring survey of fish stocks was commissioned by the ministry after local reports of declining catches.
